notes: CANONICAL entry written 2026-09-08 by this event's own initial research, promoting the proposal filed from the treasury-buyback-increase-2026-09-09 D-1 sweep. Ledger: docs/research/events/treasury-buyback-7y10y-2026-09-17.md. TWO CORRECTIONS THIS ENTRY OWNS, both from Treasury's own operations data (fiscaldata buybacks_operations + buybacks_security_details, 219 rows, fetched direct 2026-09-08). FIRST, CAP PARITY IS NOT PURCHASE PARITY — the proposal filed this event as the '$4B parity benchmark' proving sb0607 merely lifts the long end to the size the rest of the nominal curve already carried. True on caps, false on purchases. Across all nine operations this bucket has ever run it has filled its cap ZERO times, accepting a mean of $414 million and a median of $210 million, on a $4 billion cap since 2024-09-10; the 10Y-20Y bucket buys its entire $2 billion cap 21 times out of 21. On accepted par — the only number that reaches the market — the long end at its OLD cap already purchases four times what this bucket purchases at $4 billion, so sb0607 is the largest actual-purchase change in the nominal program rather than a normalization. SECOND, THE '7Y TO 10Y' LABEL IS WRONG ABOUT WHAT GETS BOUGHT: every eligible list in the three 2026 operations is ten 10-Year notes on the Feb/May/Aug/Nov cycle and contains no 7-Year note at all, which is mechanically necessary — a 7-Year note maturing inside 09/18/2033-09/17/2036 was issued 09/2026 or later and so is unissued or fails the first-coupon/on-the-run exclusions on operation day. The eligible COUNT is derivable rather than awaited: twelve quarterly 10-Year maturities sit in range, the newest two have not passed a first coupon, 12 - 2 = 10, matching 3 of 3 observed 2026 lists. Two cautions carried forward. sb0607 does NOT cover this bucket (it names the 10Y-20Y and 20Y-30Y NOMINAL sectors only), so a $4 billion print on 09-16 is the standing cap and is NOT evidence the increase took effect — that test belongs to the 09-09 announcement and the 09-10 operation. And nothing about 09-17's tape is attributable: the 10-Year TIPS auction runs 1:00pm ET forty minutes earlier, the monthly coupon announcement and housing starts share the morning, the FOMC decision landed 23.5 hours before, and opex plus the BoJ follow the next day. Estimate-labeled throughout; nothing here licenses an entry. PULSE 2026-09-10 (D-7) — THREE UPDATES THIS ENTRY OWNS. FIRST, the replacement schedule that four ledger rows recorded as unpublished posted 2026-09-09 at 09:44 ET, and it LEFT THIS ROW CHARACTER-IDENTICAL while rewriting six long-end rows (9/24, 10/1, 10/8, 10/15, 10/27, 11/4) from a hard maximum to '= or > $4 billion' — a published floor with the maximum revealed one business day ahead. 2Y-3Y (10/6) and 1Mo-2Y (11/5) keep hard figures too, so the split is long-end vs everything else, not this bucket alone. No footnote defines the new wording and no press release accompanied it (sb0607 remains the last buyback release; newest is sb0626, Iran sanctions). Treasury reopened the program's parameters and affirmatively left the belly where it was. SECOND, the cap-parity correction above now rests on a live print rather than history alone: the 2026-09-10 10Y-20Y operation accepted $5.187B against a $6B maximum — 6.2x this bucket's ENTIRE 2026 purchases ($835M) in one afternoon. THIRD, the chronic under-fill has a mechanism, and it is COVER rather than anything about the belly: across all 100 nominal liquidity-support operations ever run (2024-05-29 to 2026-09-10), no operation has ever filled its cap at cover below 1.5x (n=11, mean fill 16.9%, best 49.7%), while at cover at or above 3x it fills 60 of 64. This bucket's mean cover is 1.32x, below 1.5x in 6 of 9 operations, and the 5Y-7Y neighbour on an identical $4B cap is 0 for 8 on the same shape. Dealers under-offer; Treasury's relative-value price test then takes only the cheap tail. Confirmed out-of-sample on 09-10, when a tripled long-end cap dropped cover to 1.75x and produced that bucket's first non-full fill in 22 operations. The eligible-list derivation was also re-verified from the security universe itself (auctions_query over maturity 09/18/2033-09/17/2036 returns 18 notes: 6 TIPS on the Jan/Jul 15 cycle plus 12 nominal 10-Year notes on Feb/May/Aug/Nov; dropping the on-the-run 2036-08-15 reopened 09-09 at $39B and the 2036-05-15 whose first coupon 2026-11-15 is unpaid leaves exactly 10, 2033-11-15 to 2036-02-15) and no 7-Year note exists in the window at all. Status remains estimate for the 09-16 announcement. Still no position and nothing attributable: 09-17 also carries a $19B 10-Year TIPS reopening at 1:00pm ET (91282CRE3, maturing 2036-07-15 — inside this operation's window yet ineligible as a TIPS in a Nominal Coupons operation), the coupon announcement, housing starts, Philly Fed and the BoE, with the FOMC 23.5 hours earlier and opex plus the BoJ the next day.
